body: Fixed.
What I meant was more that `file_path` should be the `uid://` string (the one originally loaded which was getting converted). But if it works this way... 🤔

Don't use ResourceLoader to get UID. EditorFileSystem keeps UID cached for each file, so you can add `get_file_uid()` method to EditorFileSystemDirectory to return it.

(there is also a global version of this method, you should replace other ResourceLoader usages too)

Also you can do early skip here if the UID is invalid.
Do you think this could be an issue? I started like this to have the type safety point out all the occurrences, but I think its generally cleaner.
Thanks its hard to figure out which method is idiomatic. I replaced all the ResourceLoader calls.

My thought was that ResourceLoader needs a UID string to load a resource, but then remembered that it will convert it to `res://` anyway, so using the ID directly is better in the end.

The only downside is that non-resources (text files) can't be supported now.
It's not about idiomatic. Using EditorFileSystem is usually faster, because it has everything cached. It does not need to load any files or use complex systems like ResourceFormatLoaders.
But that would be the same for string UIDs right? Of course there it would be easier to optionally still use file paths. Although that also sounds dangerous.
I see 👍

All of the added includes in this PR are unnecessary and should be removed.
Might be your IDE configuration that auto-adds it.

This could be LocalVector

```suggestion
	LocalVector<ResourceUID::ID> uids;
```

```suggestion
	paths.reserve_exact(uids.size());
```
This is better if the array is not going to grow.
This should be wrapped in `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED`.

UIDs should be used only internally whenever possible, it's not useful to show one in an error message.

```suggestion
			ERR_PRINT(vformat("EditorQuickOpenDialog: No type for path %s.", ResourceUID::get_singleton()->get_id_path(p_candidate.uid)));
```
Removed.
Any reason why `_add_history_candidates()` is a separate method? It's only called once and requires adding `candidates_uids` field to the class. As a result, `existing_uids` is unused.

Performing the cleanup in this method means that the history may get validated multiple times when dialog is opened. It's unnecessary. It's only useful when a file is deleted externally while the dialog is open, which is very unlikely, and this still does not protect in every case.
This should be done after the candidate is created, otherwise the type might be added for invalid UID.
During the refactor I was under the impression that this would also be needed in the fuzzy search, but its not the case. So it can be removed again.

The file should be loaded only once, just the cleanup should be repeated.

This code does the cleanup while loading from file, so there should be another branch if dialog is opened for the second time and later.
@KoBeWi Hi, can history_file be stored using ID (int) instead of UID (String) to reduce unnecessary conversions?
@actforjason Do you mean for the history file? Within the dialog it is now stored as  ID (int) as of this pull request.

Still String UID 😕.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/60fff00a660a2aeb03f88c07fb7baed353bcb72f/editor/gui/editor_quick_open_dialog.cpp#L536
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/60fff00a660a2aeb03f88c07fb7baed353bcb72f/editor/gui/editor_quick_open_dialog.cpp#L1100

Yes, this is for the history file. I'm unsure if the int uids are persistent, otherwise it should be possible.
Is there a measurable performance hit due to these conversions?
The conversion does not matter for serialization and strings should be preferred in this case.

> Yes, this is for the history file. I'm unsure if the int uids are persistent, otherwise it should be possible. Is there a measurable performance hit due to these conversions?

It's just that I first opened Quick Open, it was a bit slow, and I'm not sure if this is related. After all, it not only processes ResourceUID::ID but also String UID.

You should do some profiling if you want to know why it's slow. I doubt it's because of UID conversions, more likely it's the container (Controls) initialization. They are created on demand, to avoid affecting editor startup time.

String UID is only used in reading and writing history_file, only id is used elsewhere, so String UID may be omitted. 
Further, there is confusion in naming, where ID is used later, but still named uid.

They don't xd
The context is different.

The UIDs stored in file are loaded only once and saved only when accepting.
The UIDs stored in memory are accessed every time the items are refreshed (so a lot).
